mcat_description.short: FRP Portable Toilet is a prefabricated, self-contained sanitation cabin made from Fibre Reinforced Plastic (FRP), sold as a ready-to-install unit with integral waste-holding or septic tank, water tap, and light point. Available in Indian-style and Western-style configurations, single or multi-compartment, for temporary or semi-permanent deployment.
mcat_description.long: FRP Portable Toilets are factory-manufactured, standalone sanitation cabins constructed from Fibre Reinforced Plastic panels, offering a lightweight, weather-resistant, and corrosion-proof alternative to brick-and-mortar toilet construction. Standard units are supplied in Indian-style (squat pan) or Western-style (commode) configurations, with typical cabin dimensions ranging from 3×3×7 ft to 4×4×8 ft, FRP wall thickness of 2–6 mm, and integral provisions for a water tap, bulb holder, and optional overhead water tank or septic tank. Multi-compartment blocks (2-in-1, 3-in-1, up to 6-in-1) combine toilet, bathroom, and urinal sections for higher-footfall deployments at construction sites, public events, and municipal installations. The Indian market is served by a large base of regional manufacturers concentrated in Maharashtra, Delhi-NCR, and Nagpur, with Sintex being the most widely recognised trade brand alongside numerous unbranded fabricators.

market_context: FRP Portable Toilets occupy a well-defined segment of India's prefabricated sanitation market, distinguished from HDPE/polyethylene portable toilets by their higher structural rigidity, thicker wall construction (2–8 mm FRP panels), and superior weather resistance. The Indian market offers two broad tiers: economy cabins (thin FRP, basic Indian pan, tap, and light point) used predominantly at construction sites and labour camps, and executive/premium cabins (thicker FRP, ceramic commode, wash basin, mirror, ventilation, and optional AC provision) used at corporate events and upscale public installations. Sintex is the dominant recognised trade brand in the Indian market, though a large number of regional unbranded fabricators — concentrated in Pune/Pimpri-Chinchwad, Nagpur, Delhi-NCR, and Ghaziabad — supply the bulk of volume. The Swachh Bharat Mission and government sanitation mandates have significantly expanded institutional demand, with bio-digester variants (no sewage connection required) gaining traction for rural and off-grid deployments. BIS standards for community and public toilets (BIS 1993 norms) govern design parameters such as cubicle size and user-to-WC ratios, though FRP portable toilets as a product category do not carry a mandatory BIS ISI mark. Key buyer decision factors are cabin dimensions, toilet type (Indian vs Western), FRP wall thickness, waste/water tank capacity, and number of compartments.
